claims.text: The as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy is in a non-equilibrium, metastable state.
The as-cast alloy has a predominantly homogeneous solid-solution microstructure with minimal intermetallic content.
Annealing near 400°C induces a diffusional transformation in the as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy.
The diffusional transformation segregates Mg and associated elements.
Annealing produces fine, dispersed Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates within the primary solid-solution matrix.
Longer annealing durations between 1 and 6 hours capture the kinetics of intermetallic nucleation and growth.
Rapid quenching preserves the annealing-induced microstructural state.
Mg-rich precipitates disrupt the initially uniform chemical distribution.
Mg-rich precipitates disrupt the continuity of elements needed to form a protective oxide scale.
The precipitates alter oxide-scale formation, adhesion, morphology, and protective character during high-temperature exposure.
Mg-rich precipitates provide localized anodic sites at precipitate–matrix interfaces.
Localized anodic sites at precipitate–matrix interfaces accelerate corrosion.
Annealed samples will have a measurably larger volume fraction of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates than the as-cast baseline.
Annealing-induced precipitation will change oxide-scale morphology and oxidation kinetics relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit increased localized corrosion, including increased pit formation at precipitate boundaries.
The alloy density remains below 6 g/cm3 under the specified annealing conditions.
Annealing near 400°C avoids complete equilibrium transformation and mechanical degradation of the microstructure.
The experiment uses the as-cast material as a control and compares it with samples annealed for multiple durations under otherwise identical conditions.
TEM, SEM, EDS, XRD, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and potentiodynamic polarization can measure the proposed microstructural, oxidation, and corrosion responses.
The hypothesis is falsified if annealing does not significantly increase Mg-rich intermetallic content or if such changes are not correlated with observable oxidation or corrosion changes.
